text:
laura: quick report - our edge starter's ESM build is causing generic overloads to become `any` in consumer editors. CJS consumers are fine. this started after we bumped tsup.

miguel: hmm, did tsup change the d.ts emit pattern? any build output you can paste?

laura: simplified repro:
```ts
// src/api.ts
export function wrap(x: string): string;
export function wrap<T>(x: T): T;
export function wrap(x: any) { return x }
```
We build to dist/esm/index.mjs and dist/cjs/index.cjs plus dist/index.d.ts. In a nodenext consumer the editor shows wrap as (x: any) => any. no tsc errors.

zara: likely resolver + d.ts naming mismatch. ESM consumers often look for index.mjs.d.ts (or consult exports map). if that's missing, tsserver falls back. what's package.json `exports` and `types`?

laura: package.json has: "exports": {"import":"./dist/esm/index.mjs","require":"./dist/cjs/index.cjs"}, "types": "dist/index.d.ts". we tried `typesVersions` but couldn't get consistent behavior across editors.

henry: two separate issues: 1) resolver lookup for ESM path; 2) impl using `any` causing d.ts widening. avoid `any` in impls if you care about overloads. change impl to generic, e.g. `function wrap<T>(x: T): T { return x as T }` and regenerate d.ts. that often preserves signatures.

miguel: also tsup/esbuild might post-process declarations or rename files for nodenext. i've fixed similar by emitting declarations to `dist/types/index.d.ts` and copying that file to `dist/esm/index.mjs.d.ts` and `dist/cjs/index.cjs.d.ts` in a postbuild step so the resolver finds a matching d.ts for both import styles.

zara: alternate approach: set `types` to `dist/types/index.d.ts` and add `typesVersions: {"*": {"*": ["dist/types/*"]}}` - TS will prefer those types. but some consumers (pnpm/monorepo) had cache/hard-resolve issues and needed a version bump to pick it up.

laura: we tried the copy approach locally and it fixed the editor. downside: more files in package and a tiny postbuild script. i'm leaning toward that for starter DX.

henry: add a CI tsd test: build package, then in a small consumer fixture `import {wrap} from '../dist/esm/index.mjs'` and assert types with tsd. that will catch regressions if tsup or tsconfig changes collapse overloads.

miguel: one more nuance: `moduleResolution: bundler` vs `nodenext`/`node` changes lookup semantics. tell contributors to use `bundler` in editor for Vite/Next parity, but CI should validate with `node` resolution against emitted artifacts. document in README.

zara: also watch for monorepo path aliases; if consumers point to src via `paths` they might bypass published types and pick up source impl with `any`. recommend pointing to `dist` during local dev or a types-only package.

types-bot: note: opened issue #678 "edge starter: ESM consumers see collapsed generics/any after tsup bump" and created branch starter/678-fix-esm-declarations.

laura: i'll send a tiny PR: postbuild copy + change impls in public surface to generic style + add tsd CI. i'll include a short README blurb about nodenext vs bundler and pnpm caveats. will ping eng-devex for review.

miguel: thanks. if you want i can add the tsd workflow snippet to the PR.

henry: tiny lint rule suggestion: `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` for exported files to prevent future accidental widening. may help.

laura: good idea. adding that to the PR as an opt-in rule for starter package. will link PR when ready. :raised_hands:
